A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIFT study. All 25 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, perturbation tests, and synthetic regression results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including the main benchmark tables and the supplementary experiments in Appendices B–G.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A's Algorithm 1 are unchanged, including low-rank weight selection, dynamic mask updates, and sparse optimizer-state storage.

E1.justification: Both versions retain identical reasoning, GLUE, code-generation, StrategyQA, Wikitext/next-token perturbation, and synthetic regression coverage, including appendix evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including Full FT, LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA, S2FT, Spectral Adapters, SpIEL, SIFT, and the alternative weight-selection methods.

E3.justification: Model configurations, rank and learning-rate searches, parameter-count matching, training budgets, metrics, and testing procedures are unchanged in Section 5 and the experimental appendices.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same perturbation tests, update-interval and rank-reduction ablations, generalization evaluations, layer analyses, structured-sparsity experiments, and toy-model analyses.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same four-random-seed statement, and Figure 3 retains its error bars. No uncertainty-reporting practices or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains LLaMA-3-8B averages of 87.88 for LIFT and 86.64 for Full FT; appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the toy-model definitions, the rank-computation rule, and Appendix H's eigenspace-alignment definition are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about principal weights, reasoning performance, memory efficiency, and reduced forgetting.

C2.justification: Interpretations in Section 7 and the appendices are unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations and open questions concerning reinforcement learning, learning dynamics, GPU acceleration, and adaptive ranks.

D1.justification: A new acknowledgement on page 10 identifies use of Dutch national e-infrastructure with SURF support under grant NWO-2023.027. This adds limited computing-infrastructure information; implementation details, hyperparameters, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the full bibliography are unchanged after matching references across page breaks. No cited works or research-positioning arguments are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short Acknowledgement section before the Impact Statement and updates the arXiv version/date strip. The remaining prose and section structure, including the appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts the Impact Statement and redistributes bibliography entries across pages 10–13. Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–17 retain their content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds attribution for computing support and slightly reflows the references. Methods, experimental evidence, explanations, and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The limited infrastructure disclosure does not meaningfully alter overall rigor, clarity, or reproducibility.
